newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam holds Hong Kong resident for smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam holds Hong Kong resident for smuggling.

text.p: Police in southern Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City have detained a Hong Kong man on charges of smuggling gold jewellery into the communist country, state media said on Tuesday.

Diplomats were unable to confirm the reports, but the English-language Vietnam News said customs officials had stopped Chung Waik Kwong on Saturday shortly after he arrived at Saigon's Tan Son Nhat airport.
The report said officers found four kg (8.8 lbs) of gold jewellery in Chung's luggage and concealed beneath his clothes. The value of the haul was put at $45,000.
The report said police believed Chung was involved in a wider smuggling racket which is under investigation.
Gold smuggling often increases ahead of the Tet lunar new year festival in Vietnam, which is one of the most active periods of the year for the domestic consumer market.
This year's Tet festival begins on February 6.
Police officials, contacted by phone, refused comment.
